text:
Alex R.: heads-up — customer `acme-reports` opened a ticket, p95/p99 jumped ~5x last 25m. They say many requests time out and some return 503. I can see spikes in request queue depth in metrics. Can someone triage? :rotating_light:

support-bot: Alert: api-requests queue depth > 120 for pool=public-hosted (30m average). p99 latency cross-checked at 1.9s -> 11.6s. Ticket: https://support.example/inc/88521

Samira: pinging eng-runtime + oncall. Do we have any autoscale events or recent deploys to this pool?

Devon: no deploys in the last hour from CI. Autoscaler notes: no new nodes added — might be hitting admission control due to concurrency caps. Looking at admission logs now.

Maria: customer-reported sample request (redacted):
```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
Content-Type: application/json
{"model":"open-redwood-13b", "input":"Summarize sales Q1"}
```
They said latency for that particular call went ~9s then 503.

Samira: can you paste the admission logs and worker queue logs? need to see if requests are getting rejected or stuck behind long-running prompts.

Devon: snippets from admission controller:
```
[admit] ts=2026-03-15T15:02:34Z pool=public-hosted in_flight=320 concurrency_limit=256 enqueueing=true
[admit] ts=2026-03-15T15:03:12Z pool=public-hosted in_flight=410 concurrency_limit=256 dropped=18 fallback_route=none
```
Also seeing worker-side backlog: `worker-7` CPU pinned, liveness steady, but KV cache pressure high — lots of long context requests.

Samira: hmm that explains p99. Concurrency limit is 256 and in_flight hit 410 => heavy queueing and admission controller started dropping. Dropped=18 explains 503s.

Alex R.: customer is on a lat-sensitive route; they expect <200ms normally. This is affecting their dashboard refresh. They asked for repro steps; we should give mitigation ASAP.

Josh: quick mitigations we can try: 1) temporarily increase concurrency limit for pool=public-hosted to 512 (risk: overload workers). 2) Route this customer to a lower-cost but higher-capacity variant (smaller model) as a fallback. 3) Enable short-circuit reply (serve cached summary) for repeated requests. I can do #2 and #3 quickly.

Maria: customer uses long contexts frequently. Might be worth enabling prefix/KV caching for their org to cut token compute. Should we propose toggle to them?

Samira: immediate action plan:
- Josh: create temporary routing rule to divert acme-reports to `open-redwood-6b` fallback and enable non-blocking fallback for 10m.
- Devon: raise concurrency limit to 384 and watch CPU/GPU utilization and per-worker queue lengths.
- Maria: ask customer for a minimal repro and sample of heavy context payloads so we can simulate locally.
- Me (Samira): keep customer updated, add runbook entries.

Devon: raising concurrency to 384 now. Monitoring: GPU util climbs from 62% -> 78% on many workers. Queue depth dropped from 120->60 over 6m. No immediate OOMs.

support-bot: Action: route change applied for org=acme-reports -> fallback=open-redwood-6b (TTL 10m).

Josh: applied fallback route and enabled cached-summary for repeated queries. Initial customer-reported path now averages ~1.1s p99.

Alex R.: thanks. Customer is getting better but still sees occasional 5s spikes. They asked whether this is a recurring pattern and if we can prevent it.

Samira: long-term suggestions to avoid backpressure: enforce client-side concurrency limits (recommend 8 concurrent requests per org by default), enable prefix/KV caching for high-context workloads, and set smart per-org token quotas to avoid noisy neighbors. Also consider autoscaler tuning: faster node spin-up and buffer headroom.

Maria: I reproduced a heavy workload locally with their sample. With naive settings, p99 jumps when more than ~200 concurrent long-context requests flood the pool. With KV caching enabled p99 improves 3x. I'll put repro steps in the ticket.

Devon: follow-up: autoscaler logs show scale decisions delayed by 30–45s due to control plane throttling under metadata churn. Filing ENG-INFRA spike ticket.

Samira: customers want an explanation. Draft reply: "We observed a transient surge of long-context requests that overwhelmed the public-hosted pool's concurrency settings. The admission controller started dropping excess requests (503) and queueing increased, causing p95/p99 regressions. We applied a temporary fallback to a compatible smaller model and increased concurrency to relieve backlog. We're following up with autoscaler and caching improvements to prevent recurrence."

Alex R.: send that. Also add CI action: add a synthetic canary that generates long-context load every 6h to validate autoscaler responsiveness.

Josh: note in ops: rollback plan if GPU memory or latencies degrade: revert concurrency change and roll back fallback routing. Monitoring alerts on per-worker GPU memory and request latency are in place.

support-bot: Ticket #88521 updated: status -> mitigated.

Samira: action items assigned: Devon -> infra ticket for autoscaler delay, Maria -> KV-caching rollout proposal + repro attachments, Josh -> follow-up with customer about fallback acceptance and opt-in caching, Alex -> coordinate canary. I'll close thread once follow-ups are in the ticket. :white_check_mark:
